name: api_getConfigurationArchiveDetails
description:
**Use Cases - Pick this tool for ANY of these question types about a device's configuration archive / archive history / configuration changes / config drift:**
- "When was the last archive of device X?" / "latest archive timestamp" / "most recent archive"
- "How many archives / config archives / configuration backups for device X?"
- "How many config drifts / configuration drifts / drift entries / drift instances on device X?"
- "Was device X changed outside Catalyst Center / outside CatC?" / "out-of-band (OOB) config changes" / "external configuration changes"
- "Who made the last config change on device X?" / "which user last modified the configuration"
- "When was the last startup config / startup-config change on device X?"
- "How many devices in site Y had config changes in the last N days/hours?"

Returns the historical device configurations (running, startup, vlan) by specified criteria. The response is an array with one entry per device. Within each device entry the `versions` array is ordered chronologically OLDEST FIRST: `versions[0]` is the EARLIEST archive for that device and `versions[-1]` (the LAST element of the array) is the MOST RECENT / LATEST archive.

**CRITICAL - How to find the LATEST archive. This applies IDENTICALLY to every phrasing that asks for the newest/last/most-recent archive, including 'when was my last archive done', 'when was the last archive', 'last archive', 'most recent archive', 'latest archive timestamp', 'last change', 'who made last config change', 'last startup-config change'. Treat ALL of these phrasings exactly the same.**

STEP 0 (MANDATORY): The `versions` array is sorted OLDEST-FIRST and the API returns only the FIRST `limit` versions. If you pass a small `limit` (e.g. 10) you will receive only the 10 OLDEST archives and the true latest will be missing. Therefore for ANY latest/last/most-recent/count/history question you MUST pass `limit` = 50 (the maximum supported) so the newest archives are included. NEVER pass limit=10 for these questions.
STEP 1: Look at every element of the `versions` array and read each element's `createdTime` (epoch ms).
STEP 2: The LATEST archive is the element with the NUMERICALLY GREATEST `createdTime`. Because the array is sorted oldest-first, this is ALWAYS the LAST element, `versions[-1]`.
STEP 3: Answer using ONLY that element. Convert and report ONLY `versions[-1].createdTime`.

HARD RULE - NEVER answer with `versions[0]`. `versions[0]` is the OLDEST archive (often `createdBy == SCHEDULED_FIRST_TIME`) and is the WRONG answer for any 'latest/last/most-recent' question. If you are about to convert or report the smallest/earliest `createdTime`, STOP — you must use the largest/last one instead. When calling a timestamp-conversion helper for a 'latest/last' question, pass ONLY the single `createdTime` value taken from the LAST element `versions[-1]`. Do not pass `versions[0].createdTime`. The total archive count for a device equals the length of its `versions` array.

**CONFIG DRIFT COUNT - how to answer 'how many config drifts / configuration drifts / drift entries / drift instances':** A config drift is simply an ARCHIVED VERSION. The drift count is the TOTAL NUMBER of elements in the `versions` array - i.e. `len(versions)` - counting EVERY version regardless of its `configChangeType` or `createdBy` (include baseline/scheduled snapshots such as `SCHEDULED_FIRST_TIME` and `SCHEDULED`, and every `IN_BAND`/`OUT_OF_BAND` change). Do NOT filter by `configChangeType`. Do NOT use `startupRunningStatus` to determine drift count - `startupRunningStatus` (IN_SYNC / OUT_OF_SYNC) only describes whether the running and startup configs match for a single archived version and is NOT the definition of a config drift; even when every version is `IN_SYNC`, each version still counts as a drift. To answer a drift-count question, report `len(versions)` (remember to fetch with `limit`=50 so all versions are included). COUNT EXACTLY: enumerate the `versions` array element-by-element (assign index 1 to the first element, 2 to the second, and so on) and report the index of the final element. Do NOT estimate or round; the answer must equal the precise number of `versions` entries returned by the API for that device. Each device entry has its OWN `versions` array - count only the `versions` of the requested device; never add the device record itself or entries from other devices to the count.

Out-of-band (OOB) changes are versions where `configChangeType == OUT_OF_BAND`; in-band changes are `IN_BAND`. The user who made a change (when available) is in `versions[*].syslogConfigEventDto[*].userName`. For startup vs running config questions, filter by `fileType` (`RUNNINGCONFIG` or `STARTUPCONFIG`). For time-window questions ('last N days/hours'), pass `createdTime` using the STRICT format `<logicalOp>:<epochMillis>` — operator, then a COLON, then EPOCH MILLISECONDS (13-digit integer). Example: `GT:1781344279000`. NEVER use a dot separator and NEVER pass an ISO/human-readable timestamp (e.g. `GT.2026-06-14T05:46:23.063000` is WRONG). Compute the cutoff instant, convert it to epoch milliseconds, then build `GT:<epochMillis>` (or `LT`/`BT` as appropriate; only GT, LT, BT are supported; `BT` takes two comma-separated epoch-ms values).

**FLEET-WIDE / 'WHICH DEVICES' TIME-WINDOW questions (e.g. 'list the devices that went through any config change in the last 12 hours', 'which devices changed in the last N days', 'how many devices had config changes recently'):** `deviceId` is OPTIONAL. For these fleet-wide questions you can call this tool with ONLY the `createdTime` filter (e.g. `createdTime='GT:<epochMillis>'`) and DO NOT pass `deviceId` unless specifically needed because of a filter. If `deviceId` filter is not provided, the API will return one entry per device that has a matching archive in that window, so a single call answers the whole question. DO NOT first fetch the device inventory / list all devices unless specific filter needs to be applied on the devices. Passing many devices makes the request URL exceed the ~2000-character safe limit and the server returns HTTP 431 'Request Header Fields Too Large' (`deviceId` is sent as a URL query parameter and is capped at 25 comma-separated UUIDs; fleet-wide queries must therefore omit it). Simply omit `deviceId` and let the time filter select the devices.

**PRE-REQUISITE - ONLY for questions scoped to a SPECIFIC named device (an IP, hostname, or serial in the question):** Call `get_device_details` first to resolve that one IP/hostname to a device UUID, then pass it as `deviceId`. Exception: if the user already supplied a valid device UUID, you may skip `get_device_details`. `deviceId` is NOT mandatory - omit it entirely for fleet-wide/time-window questions as described above; never enumerate all devices to populate it.

**Do NOT route 'config drift', 'archive history', 'OOB change', 'who changed', or 'last startup-config change' questions to `api_deviceComplianceStatus`, `api_complianceDetailsOfDevice`, `api_getNetworkDeviceConfigurationFileDetails`, or `api_countOfNetworkDeviceConfigurationFiles` — those tools are for different use cases.**

name: api_getConnectedDeviceDetail
description:
**Tool Dependency: IMPORTANT**

This tool retrieves neighbor device details for a SPECIFIC device and interface. Use this tool when user asks for neighbor/connected device information on a particular interface. The response includes neighborDevice, neighborPort, and capabilities - comprehensive neighbor device information.

**REQUIRED PRE-REQUISITES:**
- Device UUID: Retrieved from `get_device_details` tool
- Interface UUID: Retrieved from `get_interface_details` tool

You MUST call `get_device_details` and `get_interface_details` BEFORE calling `api_getConnectedDeviceDetail`. This is non-negotiable.

**Step-by-step process:**

1. First, invoke `get_device_details` with the device name or IP address to resolve the device UUID
2. Then, invoke `get_interface_details` with the device UUID and interface name to resolve the interface UUID
3. Extract both UUIDs from their respective responses
4. Finally, invoke `api_getConnectedDeviceDetail` with both the `deviceUuid` and `interfaceUuid` parameters

**Exception:**
If the user explicitly provides valid device UUID and interface UUID in their request, you may skip steps 1-2 and use the provided UUIDs directly in `api_getConnectedDeviceDetail`.

**Use Cases - Pick this tool for questions like:**
- "Get neighbor device details for device 50.40.1.45 on the interface GigabitEthernet1/0/14"
- "Show me connected device information for device core-router on interface GigabitEthernet1/0/14"
- "What devices are connected to interface GigabitEthernet1/0/14 on device 192.168.1.100"
- "Get neighbor information for device xyz on interface abc"
- "Show connected device details on this interface"

name: api_getCountOfSecurityAdvisoriesAffectingTheNetworkDevice
description:
**Tool Dependency: CRITICAL**

This tool retrieves the COUNT of security advisories, PSIRTs, and vulnerabilities affecting a specific network device. It can be called in two ways:

1. **With networkDeviceId only**: Returns the total count of ALL security advisories affecting the device
2. **With networkDeviceId AND security advisory id**: Returns whether the device is affected by a SPECIFIC advisory (acts as a filter)

**REQUIRED PRE-REQUISITE:**
You MUST call `get_device_details` BEFORE calling `api_getCountOfSecurityAdvisoriesAffectingTheNetworkDevice`. This is non-negotiable.

**Step-by-step process:**

1. First, invoke `get_device_details` with the device name or IP address to resolve the device UUID
2. Extract the UUID from the `get_device_details` response
3. Then, invoke `api_getCountOfSecurityAdvisoriesAffectingTheNetworkDevice` with:
   - `networkDeviceId` parameter set to the resolved UUID (REQUIRED)
   - `id` parameter set to specific advisory ID if you want to filter for a particular advisory (OPTIONAL)

**Exception:**
If the user explicitly provides a valid device UUID in their request, you may skip step 1 and use the provided UUID directly in `api_getCountOfSecurityAdvisoriesAffectingTheNetworkDevice`.

**Use Cases - Pick this tool for questions like:**
- "How many security advisories affecting device 50.40.1.45?" (networkDeviceId only)
- "How many security advisories affecting device core-router?" (networkDeviceId only)
- "How many CVEs affect the device core-router?" (networkDeviceId only)
- "Is device core-router affected by advisory cisco-sa-20160525-ipv6?" (networkDeviceId + id)
- "Is device 192.168.1.100 affected by advisory cisco-sa-20160525-ipv6?" (networkDeviceId + id)
- "Is device affected by advisory cisco-sa-20160525-ipv6?" (networkDeviceId + id)
- "Is device 192.168.1.100 affected by any security advisories?" (networkDeviceId only)
- "Is device edge-router-01 affected by any security advisories?" (networkDeviceId only)
- "How many vulnerabilities affect the device?" (networkDeviceId only)"

name: api_getDeviceControllabilitySettings
description: Device Controllability is a system-level process on Catalyst Center that enforces state synchronization for some device-layer features. Its purpose is to aid in the deployment of required network settings that Catalyst Center needs to manage devices. Changes are made on network devices during discovery, when adding a device to Inventory, or when assigning a device to a site. If changes are made to any settings that are under the scope of this process, these changes are applied to the network devices during the Provision and Update Telemetry Settings operations, even if Device Controllability is disabled. The following device settings will be enabled as part of Device Controllability when devices are discovered. - SNMP Credentials. - NETCONF Credentials. Subsequent to discovery, devices will be added to Inventory. The following device settings will be enabled when devices are added to inventory. - Cisco TrustSec (CTS) Credentials. The following device settings will be enabled when devices are assigned to a site. Some of these settings can be defined at a site level under Design > Network Settings > Telemetry & Wireless. - Wired Endpoint Data Collection Enablement. - Controller Certificates. - SNMP Trap Server Definitions. - Syslog Server Definitions. - Application Visibility. - Application QoS Policy. - Wireless Service Assurance (WSA). - Wireless Telemetry. - DTLS Ciphersuite. - AP Impersonation. If Device Controllability is disabled, Catalyst Center does not configure any of the preceding credentials or settings on devices during discovery, at runtime, or during site assignment. However, the telemetry settings and related configuration are pushed when the device is provisioned or when the update Telemetry Settings action is performed. Catalyst Center identifies and automatically corrects the following telemetry configuration issues on the device. - SWIM certificate issue. - IOS WLC NA certificate issue. - PKCS12 certificate issue. - IOS telemetry configuration issu

name: api_getFieldNoticeNetworkDevices
description:
Returns field notice network devices. Use this tool for questions such as 'What devices have field notices?', 'Show devices scanned for field notices.', 'Give devices with more than N notices.', 'List devices with noticeCount greater than N.', or follow-up questions asking which devices the confirmed field notices pertain to. Use this list API, not the count API, whenever the user asks to give, list, show, display, or enumerate devices, even if a noticeCount threshold is provided. An answer that includes raw device id values is invalid. Do not claim NOT_SCANNED devices have field notices. Each row in the final table MUST include only device name, management IP, and number of confirmed field notices (noticeCount). Do not include potentialNoticeCount or potential field notices unless the user explicitly asks for potential field notices.

MANDATORY POST-PROCESSING: The returned networkDeviceId is an internal device UUID for backend lookup only. For every device row that will be included in the final answer, call get_device_details with device_id set to that exact networkDeviceId value. A get_device_details call without device_id is invalid for this workflow because it returns an unrelated generic device list. Never join field-notice rows to device details by row order, offset, time range, or first returned device. If get_device_details does not return a matching device whose id equals the field-notice networkDeviceId, do not include that row in the main device table and do not infer or fabricate the device name or management IP. Instead, mention separately that some devices could not be enriched.

name: api_getFieldNoticeNetworkDevicesForTheNotice
description:
Get network devices for a specific field notice. Use this tool when the user asks which devices are affected by a specific field notice id. User-facing answers must not show raw networkDeviceId values.

MANDATORY POST-PROCESSING: The returned networkDeviceId is an internal device UUID for backend lookup only. For every device row that will be included in the final answer, call get_device_details with device_id set to that exact networkDeviceId value. A get_device_details call without device_id is invalid for this workflow because it returns an unrelated generic device list. Never join field-notice rows to device details by row order, offset, time range, or first returned device. If get_device_details does not return a matching device whose id equals the field-notice networkDeviceId, do not include that row in the main device table and do not infer or fabricate the device name or management IP.

name: api_getNetworkBugDevices
description: Get network devices that have network bugs detected by the network bug scan. Use this list tool for requests like 'what devices have bugs?', 'show all devices with network bugs', 'devices with failed bug scans', or 'devices scanned by CX Cloud'. For unqualified devices-with-bugs questions, call this tool with bugCount: 0 and limit: 10 so only devices with at least one detected bug are returned. If you need device names, IPs, models, or site details after this tool returns, call get_device_details only for the returned networkDeviceId values: use device_id for one returned ID, or filters: [{"field":"id","operator":"in","value":[...returned networkDeviceId values...]}] for multiple IDs. Step 3- Use 'GET /intent/api/v1/wired/networkDevices/{networkDeviceId}/configFeatures/intended/configurationModels/{previewActivityId}/networkDevices/{networkDeviceId}/config' to view the CLIs that will be applied to the device. name: api_retrieveTagsAssociatedWithNetworkDevices
description:
**TAG PHRASE EXCLUSION:**
- If the user starts from a named tag using `tag`, `tagged`, `with <value> tag`, `under tag`, or `in tag` and asks which/list/show/get devices or how many devices belong to that value, do not use this inverse device-to-tags tool.
- The value remains a tag name even if it looks like a switch, device, site, hostname, or operational label. Use `api_getTag` followed by `api_getTagMembersById` for lists, or `api_getTagMemberCount` for counts.

**TAG-TO-DEVICE MEMBERSHIP PROHIBITION:**
- Do not select this tool when the user starts from one named tag and asks which devices belong to it.
- Do not select this tool for counts of devices inside one named tag.
- This tool is only for the inverse direction: starting from devices and asking which tags are assigned to them.
- For tag-to-device membership, select `api_getTag` together with `api_getTagMembersById`.
- For tag-to-device counts, select `api_getTag` together with `api_getTagMemberCount`.

"What tags are assigned to devices?" "Show device-to-tag mappings" "List tags associated with network devices" — USE THIS API only for DEVICE -> TAGS direction.

This API returns which tags each network device has. It answers device-to-tag mapping questions, not tag-to-device membership questions.

**USE THIS API FOR:**
- showing tags assigned to devices
- listing device-to-tag associations
- asking what tags a device or set of devices has

**DO NOT USE THIS API FOR:**
- "List devices tagged with <tag name>"
- "Please list devices tagged <tag name>"
- "Give me the list of devices tagged with <tag name>"
- "Which devices have tag <tag name>?"
- "What devices are tagged with <tag name>?"
- "What are the devices with <tag name> tag?"
- "Get devices under tag <tag name>"
- "How many devices are tagged with <tag name>?"
- "What's the count of devices with <tag name> tag?"
- Any request that starts from one named tag and asks for its members or member count

**NEGATIVE FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES:**
- User: "Give me the list of devices tagged with <tag name>" -> do NOT use this API; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMembersById`
- User: "What devices are tagged with <tag name>?" -> do NOT use this API; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMembersById`
- User: "What are the devices with <tag name> tag?" -> do NOT use this API; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMembersById`
- User: "How many devices are tagged with <tag name>?" -> do NOT use this API; use `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMemberCount`

For named-tag membership questions, the correct route is:
1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)`
2. extract UUID
3. `api_getTagMembersById(id=<UUID>, memberType='networkdevice')`

For named-tag member-count questions, the correct route is:
1. `api_getTag(name=<tag_name>)`
2. extract UUID
3. `api_getTagMemberCount(id=<UUID>, memberType='networkdevice')`

**WRONG ROUTING TO AVOID:**
- STOP if the user names one specific tag and asks for devices in that tag.
- STOP if the user asks for the count of devices in one named tag.
- Do not substitute this API for `api_getTag` -> `api_getTagMembersById`.
- Do not combine this API with `execute_python_code` to reconstruct the members of one named tag.

description:
**Retrieves** the summary of consumed network device licenses.

Use this tool to obtain **aggregate statistics** and license usage counts by type (e.g. 'DNA Advantage' counts).

**CRITICAL INSTRUCTION: SUMMARY ONLY**
This tool returns **ONLY counts**, it does **NOT** return device lists or details. It provides high-level dashboard data.

**Do NOT:**
- Use this tool for queries asking to **list**, **show**, **find**, or **get** details of devices.
- Use this tool if the user needs to know *which* devices have a license. Use `api_readNetworkDeviceLicenses` for that purpose.

**Use Case Limitation:**
Unless the user specifically asks for 'Summary' or 'Breakdown', ALWAYS prefer `api_readNetworkDeviceLicenses` for finding devices.

DO NOT USE FOR SYSTEM-LEVEL QUERIES: This API is ONLY for network device license summaries (switches, routers, APs managed BY Catalyst Center). DO NOT use for "my system", "the system", "CatC", or "Catalyst Center platform" queries - use api_systemLicensingStatus for those instead.

**USE THIS API WHEN:**
- Query asks for network device license summary (devices managed by CatC)
- Need counts of unregistered, out-of-compliance, expired, or expiring DEVICE licenses
- Want aggregated counts of Network/DNA/CNS licenses consumed by managed network devices

**DO NOT USE THIS API WHEN:**
- "How many licenses are consumed by my system?" → api_systemLicensingStatus
- "License usage of my system" → api_systemLicensingStatus  
- "How many licenses have I consumed?" (no device specifics) → api_systemLicensingStatus
- "Show license consumption details" (no device type) → api_systemLicensingStatus
- "What licenses does my CatC use?" → api_systemLicensingStatus
- "How many purchased licenses are there for switch devices?" → api_getLicenseUsage with productFamily: SWITCH
- "How many used licenses do I have for routers?" → api_getLicenseUsage with productFamily: ROUTER
- "How many licenses are used by managed devices for WLCs?" → api_getLicenseUsage with productFamily: UNIFIED_AP
- "Show license usage for WLC device type" → api_getLicenseUsage with productFamily: UNIFIED_AP
- For purchased/used/available license totals by product family (switch/router/WLC/wireless/AP/ISE), use api_getLicenseUsage (NOT this API).

Retrieves the summary of consumed network, DNA, and unified licenses BY MANAGED NETWORK DEVICES (not the CatC system itself), along with the counts of unregistered and out-of-compliance network devices, and expired and expiring network device licenses. This is a network device aggregate view, not a system-level or account-level view.
